key_insight: Visual generators fail not because they cannot render images, but because their knowledge is fixed while the real world keeps changing. This paper proposes a search-based way to extend what visual agents can know and generate beyond their training cutoff.
problem_solved: It addresses the world-knowledge bottleneck in agentic visual generation: models are asked to create images involving new characters, trending entities, post-cutoff events, and other long-tailed concepts that were never in their training data, causing confident hallucinations.
method: Builds SearchGen-20K, a dataset of 20,839 prompts covering 12 failure categories and 22 domains.
Creates SearchGen-Bench to evaluate how well visual generation agents handle open-ended, knowledge-heavy requests.
Pairs prompts with pre-executed search information, enabling agents to retrieve missing world knowledge before generating visuals.
impact: For practitioners, this suggests a practical path to make image generation systems more reliable on real-world, evolving content. It is especially useful for building agents that must stay current without retraining on every new event or entity.

paper_title: Search Beyond What Can Be Taught: Evolving the Knowledge Boundary in Agentic Visual Generation
paper_authors: Haozhe Wang, Weijia Feng, Jinpeng Yu, Che Liu, Ping Nie
